People to hear from
• The accountant (Kostas & Reid): She has not been heard. She sets the quarter-start rule, needs two weeks and the closing trial balance, needs the rebate account kept, and quotes about AUD 5,500 plus GST. Her answer limits every date option.
• The Stirling Hotel accounts team: They have not been heard. They hold a 30-day notice right on invoice changes, their system matches invoices automatically, they have asked for a sample, and their contract price query is still open.
• The Executive Chair: He owns prices and spend over AUD 10,000 and set the switch conditions. His reasons on timing, rebates and staffing haven't been heard.
• Accounts and the invoicing backup: Month end, rebates, Friday invoicing and the recall trace all depend on them. Neither is on the interview list.
• The food-safety adviser: She must review the change before go-live and owns the repeat mock recall. She was not at the workshop.
• The dock lead and the head boner: Scale weights, lots through boning and labels are worked out in their areas.
• Harbourline's contact: We only know their ordering, invoice file, label, recall and delivery-window needs second-hand.
• The audit and risk committee chair: The committee must see the cut-over plan, which is due 4 November.
• The vendor's implementation lead: Needs to confirm the revised scope, the parallel-run approach, credit and rebate settings, and support through acceptance.
What the interviews should cover
• Why this move, and how we will know it worked (value): The CEO points to Harbourline, margin and ending re-keying. The Operations Manager points to a correct Friday dispatch and being able to trace a carton. No baseline or target is agreed for re-keying time, weight corrections or trace time.

Why this work
Replace the paper and repeated typing between orders, dock weights, invoices and credits without stopping Friday dispatch. Support the planned Harbourline supply from 1 February 2027 and the board's growth and margin goals. Discovery must establish what is needed first, what can wait and what the full move will cost. This is an interview exercise based on invented demonstration material, not verified facts about the real business.
What we know (stated by the client or the project, with who or where we are)
• Strong support in the supplied record: catch-weight lines must bill actual kilograms to two decimals; fixed packs may use Each. Credits must reverse the original unit. Jerome approves price changes. Historical invoices stay readable in the old ledger for seven years.
• Firm project conditions: Friday dispatch must continue. No big-bang weekend switch; run old and new alongside each other for at least one pay cycle. No changeover in June or July. Jordan says the pay cycle is fortnightly.
• Clear written positions, not agreed dates: Natalie wants 16 November and live progress for the board on 9 December. Jordan proposes 18 January. Nadia requires the accounting change at a BAS quarter start, naming 1 January or 1 April, and needs two weeks plus closing balances for set-up.
• Strong support: the May recall took 9 hours 30 minutes against a 4-hour target. Supplier lots lose their link to customer cartons through

The answers now support a fortnight of side-by-side working, but no date, funded first release or tested fallback is agreed. Budget coverage remains disputed, and online ordering remains an unresolved choice. Both people have follow-up answers outstanding.

For the parallel fortnight running, you mentioned comparing invoice files, scale output, and accounting entries daily. What specific differences or issues would you consider acceptable during this period, and what would be serious enough to delay the full cutover?
What the AUD 95,000 budget covers
Open
Natalie Brennan
The board-approved AUD 95,000 is all in and covers the portal, hardware, first-year fees and overlap support.
Evidence: "the board-approved number is AUD 95,000 all in." Her list includes "the portal, hardware, first-year fees and overlap support"
Jordan Hale
Treats parallel support and extra staff cover as possibly funded outside the AUD 95,000 limit, and wants the accountant to confirm whether funding is approved.
Evidence: Asked who can confirm funding outside the limit, answered "The accountant".
KOLLAB'S NEUTRAL VIEW
Neither side can be preferred yet. The approved limit is AUD 95,000 all in, but what it includes is still open and must be confirmed by the sponsor, the Chair and the accountant. One side says that limit already covers the portal, hardware, first-year fees and overlap support. The other treats parallel support and extra staff cover as possibly funded separately and asks the accountant to confirm that. An illustrative full picture in the brief is about AUD 115,500 before overlap support and staff cover, so that picture does not fit the limit, but a smaller first release might. No separate appro
Kollab is not taking a side: the evidence does not favour either view.
Decide
FOLLOW-UP QUESTIONS
ASKED OF JORDAN HALE
What do you need the accountant to confirm in writing about parallel support and extra staff cover: that they sit inside the AUD 95,000, that they have their own approved funding, or that they are not funded yet?
If the accountant says there is no approved funding outside the AUD 95,000, what change would you accept so the two-week run can still keep deliveries and billing safe?
By when do you need the accountant's answer on this funding before the two-week run starts?
Who else should receive that answer before you treat the funding point as settled?
If a required check has not passed on the day Harbourline is due to start, what should happen that day for your existing customers' deliveries and bills?
Which checks must pass before you would allow the Harbourline start?
Who should sign off each of those checks?

Natalie Brennan has been sent follow-up questions 3 times in a row. Their thread goes on. A short conversation may settle it faster.
Differing views
When people give answers that cannot both be right, Kollab records the difference here, tests each claim, and asks everyone involved a neutral follow-up question.
Fallback if the new system fails its checks during overlap or at the Harbourline start
Open
Natalie Brennan
If the new system cannot complete live orders during the overlap, daily work returns to the old system.
Evidence: "Return daily work to the old system"
Jordan Hale
If a required check fails on 1 February, delay the Harbourline start until the new system passes all checks, rather than keep the old daily process running or use another fallback.
Evidence: "Delay the Harbourline start until the new system passes all checks"
KOLLAB'S NEUTRAL VIEW
Neither side can be preferred yet. The two answers may cover different work rather than one choice. Returning daily work to the old process is about keeping existing trading going if live orders cannot be completed during the overlap. Delaying the new customer's start is about not beginning that supply until the required checks pass. The findings say both could happen, and neither is a tested plan. The old process has not been shown to meet the new customer's ordering and invoice needs, and no agreed terms show what a delay would be accepted or what it would cost. Who can stop which work, whic
Kollab is not taking a side: the evidence does not favour either view.
Decide
FOLLOW-UP QUESTIONS
ASKED OF JORDAN HALE
What do you need the accountant to confirm in writing about parallel support and extra staff cover: that they sit inside the AUD 95,000, that they have their own approved funding, or that they are not funded yet?
If the accountant says there is no approved funding outside the AUD 95,000, what change would you accept so the two-week run can still keep deliveries and billing safe?
By when do you need the accountant's answer on this funding before the two-week run starts?
Who else should receive that answer before you treat the funding point as settled?

Draft 1, answers changed since
When everyone has answered, Kollab writes one result: what the answers settle, what is assumed, what is needed, what could go wrong, what to do next, and every difference that is still open. Every statement points at the answers it rests on. Nothing is final until you approve it.

WRITTEN BY KOLLAB
The answers have changed since this was written. Draft it again to bring it up to date.
The answers now support a fortnight of side-by-side working, but no date, funded first release or tested fallback is agreed. Budget coverage remains disputed, and online ordering remains an unresolved choice. Both people have follow-up answers outstanding. The accounting quarter-start rule is a written requirement; readiness, scale booking and customer acceptance still need confirmation. These conclusions rest on the approved strategy brief, both round-three reviews and the recorded budget conflict.

When the Friday dock list reaches the office late, who normally sends the invoices?
Someone from operations or the dock.

Has the check of the dock scale, which expires on 28 November, been booked?

Which start window would you prefer for the new system?
Other--; Mon 18 Jan 2027, with two weeks in parallel before Harbourline on 1 February. I am not against it, but I do not want a big bang in the Christmas build, and Jerome wants time to sign off the price list and the team needs training time after the shutdown.
[unreadable]
Should orders and accounts move on the same date?
I need advice before deciding
[unreadable]
What would change your mind about the time window you prefer?
I am not against it, but I would need to see that the Christmas build is covered and that we have enough training time before Harbourline goes live. If Jerome wanted an earlier date, I would want two weeks in parallel first, because Friday dispatch is my name and I do not want a big bang on the dock. If the plan also showed the phones and invoices would be steady while Michael is away, that would help. Otherwise I would keep Monday 18 January 2027.
[unreadable]

None at first

Add a third truck and driver

It is mostly right, with a change

Target
Depth
Whole project
Quick
With no single target, the run reads the project's statements, conflicts, and frame. Quick is
one pass per lens, then a synthesis.
What the evidence can carry
Assumptions
Surface the unstated assumptions this depends on, and what would show each one is false.
Benchmark
Compare this to a peer practice the evidence already names, without inventing a market figure.
Reference compare
Say where two references already in the project disagree.
Root cause
Find the underlying cause of a conflict or defect, not the symptom on the surface.
Test
Say what a small pilot would have to show before this is safe to treat as decided.
Who this binds
CEO
What this commits the organisation to, and whether that is what was actually asked for.
CFO
Cost, cash timing, and the control finance would insist on before this is treated as true.
Frontline
Judge this from the person who does the work on a normal day, not from the sponsor's summary.
Product fit
Check whether this fits the product's established behaviour and rules.
How it fails
Challenge critique
Pressure-test the answer for what is weak, unsupported, or unconvincing.
Devil's advocate
Argue the strongest case against this, so a comfortable proposal has to survive a real objection.
Groupthink
Notice agreement that arrived without a recorded dissent.
Lean
Find waiting, rework, and handoffs that do not change the outcome that was asked for.
Ripple
Trace what else must change if this is accepted: data, handoffs, and people who were not in the room.
Risk
Name the failure that would hurt the client if this is wrong, and how soon it would show up.
One method, several angles
Six Hats · six angles
Look at this through the Six Hats method, one angle at a time.

thin
